arxiv-2101-03694.title: Learning to Segment Rigid Motions from Two Frames
arxiv-2101-03694.creator: Gengshan Yang 1, Deva Ramanan 1,2 1 Carnegie Mellon University, 2 Argo AI {gengshay, deva}@cs.cmu.edu
arxiv-2101-03694.description: Abstract Appearance-based detectors achieve remarkable performance on common scenes, benefiting from high-capacity models and massive annotated data, but tend to fail for scenarios lack of training data. Geometric motion segmentation algorithms, however, generalize to novel scenes, but have yet to achieve comparable performance to appearance-based ones, due to noisy motion estimations and degenerate motion configurations.

arxiv-2303-16124.description: Abstract Context. Lithium-rich giant stars are rare and their existence challenges our understanding of stellar structure and evolution. In particular, open clusters constrain well the mass and age of their members, and therefore, offer a unique opportunity to understand the evolutionary stage where Li enrichment occurs. Aims.

arxiv-2304-04425.title: Entangled Pair Resource Allocation under Uncertain Fidelity Requirements
arxiv-2304-04425.creator: Rakpong Kaewpuang 1 , Minrui Xu 1 , Stephen John Turner 2 , Dusit Niyato 1 , Han Yu 1 , and Dong In Kim 3
arxiv-2304-04425.description: Abstract In quantum networks, effective entanglement routing facilitates remote entanglement communication between quantum source and quantum destination nodes. Unlike routing in classical networks, entanglement routing in quantum networks must consider the quality of entanglement qubits (i.e., entanglement fidelity), presenting a challenge in ensuring entanglement fidelity over extended distances.

arxiv-2312-15682.title: A Grating Based High-Frequency Motion Stimulus Paradigm for Steady-State Motion Visual Evoked Potentials
arxiv-2312-15682.creator: Bartu Atabek, Efecan Yılmaz, Cengiz Acartürk, Murat Perit Çakır
arxiv-2312-15682.description: Abstract Objective: This paper proposes a novel type of stimulus in the shape of sinusoidal gratings displayed with an imperceptibly high-frequency motion. The stimulus has been designed for use in BCI (Brain Computer Interface) applications that employ visually evoked potentials (VEPs) in an effort to mitigate discomfort associated with VEPs.

arxiv-2410-05750.title: Polynomial Time Cryptanalytic Extraction of Deep Neural Networks in the Hard-Label Setting
arxiv-2410-05750.creator: Nicholas Carlini, Jorge Chávez-Saab, Anna Hambitzer, Francisco Rodríguez-Henríquez, Adi Shamir ✉
arxiv-2410-05750.description: Abstract Deep neural networks (DNNs) are valuable assets, yet their public accessibility raises security concerns about parameter extraction by malicious actors. Recent work by Carlini et al. (Crypto’20) and Canales-Martínez et al. (Eurocrypt’24) has drawn parallels between this issue and block cipher key extraction via chosen plaintext attacks.

arxiv-2601-07338.title: Beyond Literal Mapping: Benchmarking and Improving Non-Literal Translation Evaluation
arxiv-2601-07338.creator: Yanzhi Tian Cunxiang Wang Zeming Liu Heyan Huang, Wenbo Yu Dawei Song Jie Tang Yuhang Guo
arxiv-2601-07338.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced Machine Translation (MT), applying them to linguistically complex domains—such as Social Network Services, literature etc. In these scenarios, translations often require handling non-literal expressions, leading to the inaccuracy of MT metrics. To systematically investigate the reliability of MT metrics, we first curate a meta-evaluation dataset focused on non-literal translations, namely MENT .

arxiv-2601-21846.title: Optimal Energy-Aware Service Management in Future Networks with a Gamified Incentives Mechanism
arxiv-2601-21846.creator: Konstantinos Varsos, Adamantia Stamou, George D. Stamoulis, Vasillios A. Siris
arxiv-2601-21846.description: Abstract As energy demands surge across ICT infrastructures, service providers must engage users in sustainable practices while maintaining the Quality of Experience (QoE) at acceptable levels. In this paper, we introduce such an approach, leveraging gamified incentives and a model for user’s acceptance on incentives, thus encouraging energy-efficient behaviors such as adaptive bitrate streaming.

arxiv-2602-11244.title: Stress Tests RE VE AL Fragile Temporal and Visual Grounding in Video-Language Models
arxiv-2602-11244.creator: Sethuraman T V, Savya Khosla, Aditi Tiwari, Vidya Ganesh, Rakshana Jayaprakash, [2pt] Aditya Jain, Vignesh Srinivasakumar, Onkar Kishor Susladkar, Srinidhi Sunkara, [2pt] Aditya Shanmugham, Rakesh Vaideeswaran, Abbaas Alif Mohamed Nishar, [2pt] Simon Jenni, Derek Hoiem, [5pt] University of Illinois
arxiv-2602-11244.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Sethuraman T V, Savya Khosla, Aditi Tiwari, Vidya Ganesh, Rakshana Jayaprakash, [2pt] Aditya Jain, Vignesh Srinivasakumar, Onkar Kishor Susladkar, Srinidhi Sunkara, [2pt] Aditya Shanmugham, Rakesh Vaideeswaran, Abbaas Alif Mohamed Nishar, [2pt] Simon Jenni, Derek Hoiem, [5pt] University of Illinois . This work investigates a fundamental question: Do Video-Language Models (VidLMs) robustly account for video content, temporal sequence, and motion? Our investigation shows that, surprisingly, they often do not .

pmc-11455946.title: A dataset of floating debris accumulation at bridges after July 2021 flood in Germany and Belgium
pmc-11455946.creator: Sébastien Erpicum, Daan Poppema, Lisa Burghardt, Loïc Benet, Davide Wüthrich, Elena-Maria Klopries, Benjamin Dewals
pmc-11455946.description: This paper presents a dataset documenting 71 floating debris accumulations at bridges following an extreme hydrological event that hit Belgium and Germany in July 2021. Data were collected from various sources including public authorities’ documents, public online databases, post event pictures and field visits. The dataset covers bridges geometry, flood conditions and debris accumulation.

pmc-11611777.title: A combination of lymphatic drug delivery of anti‐CTLA‐4 antibody and local radiotherapy for solid‐tumor treatment
pmc-11611777.creator: Koki Takagi, Ariunbuyan Sukhbaatar, Yohei Inaba, Shiro Mori, Tetsuya Kodama
pmc-11611777.description: The combination of radiotherapy and immunotherapy is a promising approach that has been shown in clinical trials to improve significantly survival and response rates compared with monotherapy against solid tumor. Since anti‐CTLA‐4 antibodies block immunosuppressive signals mainly in the lymph nodes (LNs), efficient drug delivery to the lymphatic system is desirable.

pmc-11963948.title: Impact of the Aortomitral Positional Anatomy on Atrioventricular Conduction Disorder Following Mitral Valve Surgery
pmc-11963948.creator: Kazuma Handa, Masashi Kawamura, Daisuke Yoshioka, Shunsuke Saito, Takuji Kawamura, Ai Kawamura, Yusuke Misumi, Masaki Taira, Kazuo Shimamura, Sho Komukai, Tetsuhisa Kitamura, Shigeru Miyagawa
pmc-11963948.description: BackgroundVariations in the aortomitral positional anatomy, including aortic root rotation appear to be related to variations in the location of the conduction system, including the bundle of His. However, little is known about their clinical significance.Methods and ResultsThis study included 147 patients with normal ECGs who underwent mitral valve surgery.

pmc-12932361.title: d-Dimer levels during pregnancy and postpartum: non-applicability of regularly used cut-offs for diagnosis of suspected pulmonary embolism
pmc-12932361.creator: E Ranieri, W Korte, G Brandi, S Kalimeris, N Ochsenbein, C Haslinger
pmc-12932361.description: PurposeTo assess d-dimer levels during pregnancy and postpartum period and evaluate the appropriateness of commonly used cut-offs for ruling out pulmonary embolism (PE) in this population.MethodsSecondary analysis of the prospective PPH 1300 study conducted at the University Hospital Zurich, including 1309 women between 25 + 0 and 42 + 3 weeks of gestation without acute thromboembolic events.

pmc-13233524.title: The theory of tumor immuno-ecodynamics
pmc-13233524.creator: Xiaoping Chen
pmc-13233524.description: BackgroundIn previous studies, I established theoretical frameworks for immunodynamics and tumor ecodynamics, respectively, to quantitatively describe immune responses and the interactions between the immune system and the tumor ecosystem. Although these two theories are closely related, they are still distinct.

pmc-13407204.title: Effects of short-term air pollution exposure on respiratory infection-related healthcare burden in kidney transplant recipients
pmc-13407204.creator: Jie JIANG, Ying ZHANG, Bo PENG, Yi ZHU, Yingzi MING, Xufang WU
pmc-13407204.description: ObjectiveKidney transplant recipients are highly susceptible to respiratory tract infections (RTIs), and short-term exposure to ambient air pollution may aggravate their clinical outcomes. However, evidence regarding the effects of specific pollutants on hospitalization burden in this population remains limited. This study aims to investigate the effects of pollutants such as PM2.5 on hospitalization burden after RTIs in kidney transplant recipients.

pmc-13476680.title: Self-Management Ability and Its Associations with Pruritus Severity, Self-Perceived Burden, and Psychological Resilience in Adults with Atopic Dermatitis: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13476680.creator: Qin Zou, Jihui Chen, Weihao Zhang, Hui Gou
pmc-13476680.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo evaluate self-management ability among adults with atopic dermatitis (AD) and examine its associations with pruritus severity, self-perceived burden, and psychological resilience.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 585 adults with AD. Self-management, pruritus, self-perceived burden, and psychological resilience were assessed using the Chronic Disease Self-Management Study Measures (CDSMS), pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), Self-Perceived Burden Scale (SPBS), and Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), respectively.
